combat_tables.description: Attack resolution tables for Star Trek tabletop games. Adapted from Star Trek Adventures (2d20 RPG) and Star Fleet Battles mechanics.

ground_combat.description: Ground combat uses the 2d20 Outcome Table with Action Dice for damage severity.

outcome_table.description: Roll 2d20 and compare the results. The highest die is the 'High Die' and the lowest is the 'Low Die'.

critical_failure.result: 1 Complication + 1 Threat — the action fails catastrophically with additional negative consequences

failure.condition: High die is 1 (but not both), or both dice are equal and ≤10
failure.result: 1 Threat — the action fails with a negative side effect

partial_success.condition: No special conditions met; total meets or exceeds TN
partial_success.result: 1 Success — the action succeeds without additional effects

success.condition: High die is 20 (but not both), or both dice are equal and ≥11
success.result: 1 Success + 1 Advantage — the action succeeds with a positive side effect

critical_success.result: 1 Success + 2 Advantages — the action succeeds spectacularly

action_dice_results.description: When an attack hits, roll the weapon's Action Dice (d6s) to determine damage severity.

phaser_stun.2: Target is stunned and drops to one knee
phaser_stun.4: Target is unconscious for 2d6 rounds; risk of Trauma
phaser_stun.5-6: Target is unconscious for 1d10 rounds; roll for Trauma

cover_modifiers.light_cover: +2 to defense roll (crates, rubble, partial walls)
cover_modifiers.heavy_cover: +4 to defense roll (bulkheads, reinforced walls, behind cover with firing port)

range_modifiers.short_range: Within weapon's short range; no modifier
range_modifiers.medium_range: Within weapon's medium range; +2 to TN
range_modifiers.long_range: Within weapon's long range; +4 to TN
range_modifiers.beyond_range: Target is beyond effective range; +6 to TN and attacker is at the target's mercy

space_combat.description: Space combat uses firing numbers, evasion, and damage tables for ship-to-ship combat.

firing_resolution.description: To hit a target, roll 2d6 and add the firing ship's weapon factor. If the total meets or exceeds the target's evasion number, the attack hits.
steps: Declare target and weapon arc (Forward, Aft, Broadside)
Check range: weapon must be within effective range
Roll 2d6 + weapon factor vs target evasion number
On a hit, roll damage on the appropriate table
Apply damage to shields first, then hull

phaser_damage_table.description: When phasers hit, roll 2d6 and add the phaser bank's power factor to determine damage.

damage_scale.1-2: Negligible — 1 hull point or shield point
damage_scale.3-4: Light — 2 hull points or shield points
damage_scale.5-6: Moderate — 3 hull points or shield points
damage_scale.7-8: Significant — 4 hull points or shield points
damage_scale.9-10: Heavy — 5 hull points or shield points
damage_scale.11-12: Severe — 6 hull points or shield points
damage_scale.13-14: Critical — 8 hull points or shield points + possible system disruption
damage_scale.15-16: Devastating — 10 hull points or shield points + system disruption
damage_scale.17-18: Catastrophic — 12 hull points or shield points + system destruction

torpedo_damage_table.description: Photon and quantum torpedoes deal massive damage. Roll on the table based on torpedo type.

photon_torpedo.6-7: Moderate damage — 12 hull points + 1 system disruption
photon_torpedo.8-9: Heavy damage — 16 hull points + 1 system disruption
photon_torpedo.10-11: Severe damage — 20 hull points + 2 system disruptions
photon_torpedo.12-13: Critical hit — 25 hull points + 2 system disruptions + possible crew casualty
photon_torpedo.14-15: Catastrophic — 30 hull points + 3 system disruptions + crew casualty
photon_torpedo.16-17: Magazine penetration — 40 hull points + possible ship destruction
photon_torpedo.18: Direct hit on command center — 50 hull points + bridge casualty

quantum_torpedo.description: Quantum torpedoes deal 1.5x the damage of photon torpedoes (round up).
quantum_torpedo.modifier: Multiply photon torpedo result by 1.5 and round up

shield_modulation.description: Ships can modulate their shields to reduce incoming damage from specific attack types.
effects: Phaser resistance: -1 to phaser damage rolls
Torpedo resistance: -2 to torpedo damage rolls
Directional focus: Double shield strength in one arc, halve in others
Shield inversion: Temporarily move shields inside the hull for 1 impulse; next hit does double damage to attacker

evasion_numbers.description: Each ship class has a base evasion number that represents how hard it is to hit.

system_disruption_table.description: When a hit causes system disruption, roll d10 to determine which system is affected.

roll.1: Warp drive — ship cannot use warp for 1d4 impulses
roll.2: Impulse drive — ship cannot maneuver at sublight for 1d4 impulses
roll.3: Forward phasers — forward phaser bank offline for 1d4 impulses
roll.4: Aft phasers — aft phaser bank offline for 1d4 impulses
roll.5: Broadside phasers — broadside phaser bank offline for 1d4 impulses
roll.6: Torpedo launchers — cannot fire torpedoes for 1d4 impulses
roll.7: Shield generator — shields offline for 1d4 impulses
roll.8: Sensors — reduced sensor range for 1d4 impulses
roll.10: Life support — crew takes 1 Stress per impulse until repaired

rpg_combat.description: RPG combat uses the 2d20 system with Action Dice for damage and stress.

steps: Attacker rolls 2d20 + Attribute + Skill vs TN
If the attack succeeds, roll the weapon's Action Dice
Apply the result to the target's Stress track first
When Stress is full, excess becomes Damage
When Damage equals Toughness, the character is incapacitated

active_defense.description: A target can attempt an Active Defense to reduce or negate incoming damage.
active_defense.mechanic: Roll Agility + Athletics vs the attacker's total (2d20 + Attribute + Skill)
active_defense.success: For each Success on the defense, negate 1 Success from the attack
active_defense.critical_defense: On a Critical Success, the defender negates all damage and gains 1 Advantage

stress.description: Temporary damage track; represents fatigue, minor wounds, and shock.
stress.capacity: Equal to the character's Toughness (Brawn + Resilience)
stress.recovery: Stress recovers during rest or medical treatment

damage.description: Permanent damage track; represents serious injuries.
damage.capacity: Equal to the character's Toughness (Brawn + Resilience)
damage.recovery: Requires medical treatment and extended downtime

trauma.description: When a character would take Damage beyond their capacity, they take Trauma instead.
effects: Physical Trauma: -1 to all physical Attribute rolls until healed
Psychological Trauma: -1 to all mental Attribute rolls until healed
Each Trauma adds a permanent limitation until resolved through therapy or significant events

ship_combat_rpg.description: Starship combat in the RPG uses the same 2d20 system with ship statistics.

ship_statistics.hull: Represents the ship's structural integrity; derived from the ship's size and construction
ship_statistics.shields: Represents the ship's deflector shield strength; regenerates when not under fire
ship_statistics.maneuverability: How well the ship can dodge attacks; modifies evasion
ship_statistics.sensors: Detection range and accuracy; modifies first strike and targeting
ship_statistics.weapons: Phaser and torpedo firepower; determines damage potential

combat_round.description: Each combat round represents several minutes of ship-to-ship combat.
phases: Maneuver: Helm officer rolls Starship Operations to position the ship
Weapons: Tactical officer rolls Weapon Skill to fire phasers or torpedoes
Defense: Science officer rolls Science to modulate shields
Repair: Engineering officer rolls Engineering to repair damage

ship_damage.description: Ships have Stress and Damage tracks similar to characters.
ship_damage.stress: Hull Stress — represents minor damage and system strain
ship_damage.damage: Hull Damage — represents serious structural damage
critical_systems: Warp Drive: If destroyed, the ship cannot travel at FTL
Impulse Drive: If destroyed, the ship cannot maneuver at sublight
Shields: If destroyed, the ship is vulnerable to direct hits
Weapons: If destroyed, the ship cannot fight back
Life Support: If destroyed, crew takes Stress each round
